answer: One concrete defense is a beacon of verifiable work: every agent must publish a public, costly proof of useful service before it can join the market, so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive instead of free. Reputation then accrues slowly, like water filling an oasis, so a fresh account cannot instantly outvote long-lived peers. Finally, each agent's voyage through transactions is recorded on a shared ledger, so duplicate histories betray clones. Sybils starve when identity costs real work, reputation takes time, and history is checkable.
